pathway.title: MAGNITE, INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Magnite's capital structure is the simplest part of the credit. Since the convertible senior notes were repaid from cash at maturity on March 15, 2026, the only debt is the 2024 term loan, with principal of USD 357,730 thousand at September 30, 2026, scheduled amortization of USD 3,632 thousand a year, and USD 342,294 thousand falling due after 2030, at the February 2031 maturity [CP-1]. The USD 175.0 million revolver matures in February 2029, was undrawn at every 2026 quarter end, and had USD 170.9 million available after USD 4.1 million of letters of credit. The October 7, 2026 repricing, a subsequent event, cut the term loan margin to Term SOFR plus 2.50%; at the September 30, 2026 principal that is roughly USD 1,789 thousand a year of lower interest before changes in Term SOFR [CP-1, calculation 11].

Earnings have improved sharply. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 is USD 280,586 thousand against USD 232,131 thousand for FY2025, and Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 10.98x [CP-1]. That figure is the issuer's own measure and adds back stock-based compensation; on income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, gross leverage is 1.81x, still low [CP-1]. Reported net income for FY2025 includes a one-off tax benefit of USD 73,986 thousand and should not be read as run-rate.

Cash is the item most open to misreading. The company collects from buyers and pays sellers, and the filing states that "in the event a buyer defaults on payment, we may still be required to pay sellers for the inventory purchased" [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Two buyers made up 40% and 12% of receivables at December 31, 2025 [CP-1A]. Cash fell from USD 553,362 thousand at FY2025 to USD 184,648 thousand at the end of the first quarter, helped by the USD 205,067 thousand note repayment and a negative first-quarter operating cash flow, before recovering to USD 392,862 thousand [CP-1]. Net debt of USD -35,132 thousand is therefore a point-in-time figure, not a permanent surplus.

The leverage covenant is a springing test: First Lien Net Leverage Ratio below 3.25 to 1.00, tested at quarter end only if revolver utilization exceeds 35% of commitments [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Thirty-five percent of USD 175.0 million is USD 61,250 thousand; the USD 60.0 million drawn and repaid within the second quarter of 2026 was just below that level, and whether letters of credit count toward utilization is not stated in the supplied text. Nothing was drawn at quarter end, so the test did not apply. As an indicator only, not the covenant calculation, first-lien debt at the term loan principal would reach 3.25x of LTM Adjusted EBITDA only if that EBITDA fell by about 61%, with cash netting and the covenant EBITDA definition both unknown [CP-0].

Claims outside the debt figure are modest on the evidence: lease liabilities of USD 21,558 thousand current and USD 40,436 thousand non-current, and non-cancelable cloud, software and data center commitments of USD 115,219 thousand, of which USD 78,343 thousand falls in 2027 [CP-1, Q3 2026 10-Q]. No pension, factoring or consent-decree obligation was found in the sections read. The Google lawsuit is a possible recovery, with nothing recorded, and the court's September 2026 remedies are under appeal [CP-1A]; guidance for 2027 excludes any upside from them.

Management's board-approved repurchase plan has USD 144.9 million of authorization left [Q3 2026 10-Q], and USD 55,559 thousand of treasury stock was purchased in the nine months to September 30, 2026 [Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement]. This is the main route by which cash could leave the credit; the restricted-payment limits in the credit agreement are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1A].

runs.text: The main strengths are balance-sheet capacity and growth momentum. Gross leverage of 1.27x on Adjusted EBITDA, net cash after the March 2026 repayment, an undrawn USD 175.0 million revolver, no maturity before 2029 and interest cover of 10.98x leave wide room against the one springing covenant [CP-1]. Operating momentum is strong: Contribution ex-TAC for nine months 2026 was USD 551,127 thousand against USD 474,583 thousand a year earlier, led by connected TV [CP-1]. The absence of a financial sponsor, dividends or debt-funded distributions in the sources read, and the repayment of the convertible notes without new borrowing, are supportive behaviours [CP-1A]. The Google ruling is a potential tailwind to open-web display share, though it is management's expectation, unquantified and under appeal.

The main weaknesses are cyclicality, concentration and unverified terms. Revenue is a percentage of ad spend, with lower fees on connected TV reserve auctions, so growth in the fastest channel can dilute the fee rate [CP-1A]. Demand is concentrated in a few platforms and two buyers hold over half of receivables, so a payment delay or loss would hit revenue and cash together. Cash includes publisher and customer float, seasonality lifts the fourth quarter, and first-quarter cash flow can be negative [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock compensation of USD 76,648 thousand in FY2025. The credit agreement, covenant definitions, restricted-payment capacity, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so legal capacity to add debt or distribute cash cannot be tested [CP-0, CP-1A]. Business is one segment, so no other activity offsets a weak ad market.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction, merger, dividend recapitalisation or new debt issue is described in the supplied sources for FY2025 or 2026 to date, other than the items below. Where a transaction source is missing for a topic, the topic is Insufficient Information rather than an adverse conclusion.

- Financing of SpotX: the 10-K risk factor states "significantly increased our leverage, which may put us at greater risk of defaulting on our debt obligations" and that the cash portion of the acquisition was financed by a term loan and convertible senior notes (10K p63). The acquisition date is not stated in the chunks read; treat it as Not supplied here. - February 6, 2024: refinancing into the 2024 Credit Agreement, a seven-year term loan and a five-year revolver (Q3Q p19). Amendments in September 2024 and March 2025 repriced the term loan to Term SOFR plus 3.00% (Q3Q p19). These are borrower-favourable repricings; they are debt terms, not changes of control. - September 2025: completed the acquisition of Streamrai, Inc., a generative-AI video-ad tool for connected TV (10K p15). The cash outflow was small relative to the balance sheet (financial base handoff, acquisitions line); purchase terms and price allocation are Not supplied in the chunks read. - September 16, 2025: filed a lawsuit against Google in the Eastern District of Virginia seeking damages and other remedies; no recovery is recorded and none is quantified (Q3Q p24, p36). - March 15, 2026: the convertible senior notes matured and were repaid in cash; no convertible notes remain (Q3Q p14). No new debt was raised for this. - Second quarter 2026: a short-term draw on the revolver was borrowed and repaid within the quarter (Q2Q p18); the revolver was undrawn at quarter ends. - February 23, 2026 and nine months 2026: the board approved a share repurchase plan, and shares were repurchased under it in the period (Q3Q p50). This returns cash to equity holders; the repurchase capacity under the credit agreement is Not supplied. - September 2026: the Court issued its remedies opinion against Google ("mandating that Google undertake certain behavioral remedies and appointing a six-year independent compliance monitor"); "Google has indicated its intent to appeal the decision" (Q3Q p36). Management says it expects "a significant positive impact on our industry and business prospects" (Management Language, Q3Q p36). The 2027 outlook is stated "not including upside from Google remedies" (ER3 p1). - Subsequent event, October 7, 2026: Amendment No. 3 lowered the term loan margin and the revolver margin range (Q3Q p29). It post-dates the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not folded into that period's facts.

Governance and sponsor behaviour (issuer level, documented actions only): the repayment of the convertible notes from cash is deleveraging; share repurchases and the prior-period repricings are neutral to supportive; there is no evidence of dividend recapitalisation, debt-funded distribution, priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release in the sources read. Legal capacity (what the credit agreement permits for restricted payments, incurrence and liens), willingness (what was done) and feasibility (liquidity and leverage in the financial base) are kept separate: willingness and feasibility are evidenced, legal capacity is not because the credit agreement is Not supplied. Evidence quality is High for the dated filings and Low for management claims in the releases.

Conflicts logged: none. No two supplied documents state a different amount or date for the same fact in the chunks read. The FY2025 10-K debt note first states a 4.50% term loan margin and then the amendments that reduced it to 3.00%; that is a history of terms, not a conflict.

fields.value: Magnite is a public company with no financial sponsor, no controlling holder identified in the supplied sources and a single operating segment. It sells technology that lets publishers, especially connected TV owners, monetize ad inventory to buyers and demand-side platforms, and earns a fee that is a percentage of the ad spend. The credit-relevant business facts are the dependence on a small number of large demand sources, the concentration of connected TV supply in a few large sellers, the lower fees on reserve auctions, seasonal fourth-quarter strength, and the effect of the Google antitrust ruling on open-web display competition. The credit-relevant history is the financing of the SpotX acquisition by a term loan and convertible notes, the 2024 refinancing and repricings, the repayment of the convertible notes in cash at maturity in March 2026, and the October 2026 repricing amendment. There is no pending acquisition, sponsor transaction or new debt issue in the supplied sources. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: deleveraging by repayment, share repurchases under a board plan and no dividends. The financial consequences are in the accepted financial base handoff; the main limits here are that ownership percentages, the proxy statement and the executed financing documents are not supplied, and that operating claims in the releases are management language.

fields.value: Magnite's capital structure is the simplest part of the credit. Since the convertible senior notes were repaid from cash at maturity on March 15, 2026, the only debt is the 2024 term loan, with principal of USD 357,730 thousand at September 30, 2026, scheduled amortization of USD 3,632 thousand a year, and USD 342,294 thousand falling due after 2030, at the February 2031 maturity [CP-1]. The USD 175.0 million revolver matures in February 2029, was undrawn at every 2026 quarter end, and had USD 170.9 million available after USD 4.1 million of letters of credit. The October 7, 2026 repricing, a subsequent event, cut the term loan margin to Term SOFR plus 2.50%; at the September 30, 2026 principal that is roughly USD 1,789 thousand a year of lower interest before changes in Term SOFR [CP-1, calculation 11].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings have improved sharply. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 is USD 280,586 thousand against USD 232,131 thousand for FY2025, and Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 10.98x [CP-1]. That figure is the issuer's own measure and adds back stock-based compensation; on income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, gross leverage is 1.81x, still low [CP-1]. Reported net income for FY2025 includes a one-off tax benefit of USD 73,986 thousand and should not be read as run-rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash is the item most open to misreading. The company collects from buyers and pays sellers, and the filing states that "in the event a buyer defaults on payment, we may still be required to pay sellers for the inventory purchased" [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Two buyers made up 40% and 12% of receivables at December 31, 2025 [CP-1A]. Cash fell from USD 553,362 thousand at FY2025 to USD 184,648 thousand at the end of the first quarter, helped by the USD 205,067 thousand note repayment and a negative first-quarter operating cash flow, before recovering to USD 392,862 thousand [CP-1]. Net debt of USD -35,132 thousand is therefore a point-in-time figure, not a permanent surplus.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The leverage covenant is a springing test: First Lien Net Leverage Ratio below 3.25 to 1.00, tested at quarter end only if revolver utilization exceeds 35% of commitments [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Thirty-five percent of USD 175.0 million is USD 61,250 thousand; the USD 60.0 million drawn and repaid within the second quarter of 2026 was just below that level, and whether letters of credit count toward utilization is not stated in the supplied text. Nothing was drawn at quarter end, so the test did not apply. As an indicator only, not the covenant calculation, first-lien debt at the term loan principal would reach 3.25x of LTM Adjusted EBITDA only if that EBITDA fell by about 61%, with cash netting and the covenant EBITDA definition both unknown [CP-0].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are modest on the evidence: lease liabilities of USD 21,558 thousand current and USD 40,436 thousand non-current, and non-cancelable cloud, software and data center commitments of USD 115,219 thousand, of which USD 78,343 thousand falls in 2027 [CP-1, Q3 2026 10-Q]. No pension, factoring or consent-decree obligation was found in the sections read. The Google lawsuit is a possible recovery, with nothing recorded, and the court's September 2026 remedies are under appeal [CP-1A]; guidance for 2027 excludes any upside from them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's board-approved repurchase plan has USD 144.9 million of authorization left [Q3 2026 10-Q], and USD 55,559 thousand of treasury stock was purchased in the nine months to September 30, 2026 [Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement]. This is the main route by which cash could leave the credit; the restricted-payment limits in the credit agreement are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strengths are balance-sheet capacity and growth momentum. Gross leverage of 1.27x on Adjusted EBITDA, net cash after the March 2026 repayment, an undrawn USD 175.0 million revolver, no maturity before 2029 and interest cover of 10.98x leave wide room against the one springing covenant [CP-1]. Operating momentum is strong: Contribution ex-TAC for nine months 2026 was USD 551,127 thousand against USD 474,583 thousand a year earlier, led by connected TV [CP-1]. The absence of a financial sponsor, dividends or debt-funded distributions in the sources read, and the repayment of the convertible notes without new borrowing, are supportive behaviours [CP-1A]. The Google ruling is a potential tailwind to open-web display share, though it is management's expectation, unquantified and under appeal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are cyclicality, concentration and unverified terms. Revenue is a percentage of ad spend, with lower fees on connected TV reserve auctions, so growth in the fastest channel can dilute the fee rate [CP-1A]. Demand is concentrated in a few platforms and two buyers hold over half of receivables, so a payment delay or loss would hit revenue and cash together. Cash includes publisher and customer float, seasonality lifts the fourth quarter, and first-quarter cash flow can be negative [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock compensation of USD 76,648 thousand in FY2025. The credit agreement, covenant definitions, restricted-payment capacity, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so legal capacity to add debt or distribute cash cannot be tested [CP-0, CP-1A]. Business is one segment, so no other activity offsets a weak ad market.
